# Identifiers and scope {#sec-dd-identifiers}


::: {.cell}

:::


## Overview

These columns identify each row of the vehicle table and record why the
vehicle is in it.

- **`vehicle_id`** is the row number in the input file supplied by the Bristol
  team. It is unique within one version of the data but **not stable between
  versions**: a new delivery renumbers the vehicles (@sec-pitfalls). To follow
  a vehicle across versions, join on the registration instead
  (@sec-dd-registration).
- **`dup_vrm`** flags a DVSA registration that appears on more than one row.
  Duplicates are kept and flagged rather than dropped, because it is not known
  which row is right.
- **The `scope_` flags** record the evidence that the vehicle existed at some
  point from 2005. A vehicle is kept if any of the four is `TRUE`; the
  138.2 million input rows become
  93.4 million in-scope vehicles. The flags are not exclusive,
  and a vehicle often meets several.

How identifiers are assigned is set out in the methodology,
[section 3.1](../../reports/methodology.md#identifiers-and-duplicates), and the
scope rules in [section 3.4](../../reports/methodology.md#scope-which-vehicles-are-kept).
@sec-pipeline explains why the table keeps vehicles for which little is known.


::: {#tbl-dd-identifiers .cell layout-align="center" tbl-cap='Identifier and scope columns.'}
::: {.cell-output-display}


|Column                |Type    |Source   |Description                                                                                                   |Missing |
|:---------------------|:-------|:--------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------|
|`vehicle_id`          |BIGINT  |pipeline |Row number in the Bristol input file (stable id for this input)                                               |0%      |
|`dup_vrm`             |BOOLEAN |pipeline |TRUE if the DVSA registration appears on more than one row of the input                                       |0%      |
|`scope_mileage`       |BOOLEAN |pipeline |In scope because total mileage > 0                                                                            |0%      |
|`scope_pca`           |BOOLEAN |pipeline |In scope because a PCA is recorded in at least one year                                                       |0%      |
|`scope_born`          |BOOLEAN |pipeline |In scope because birth_date is on or after the scope start date                                               |0%      |
|`scope_dvla_activity` |BOOLEAN |pipeline |In scope because of DVLA activity (tax due, V5C, MOT expiry or first registration) since the scope start date |0%      |


:::
:::


## Coverage

Every column in this group has a value for every vehicle. What varies over
time is the reason a vehicle is in scope, shown in @fig-dd-scope. Vehicles
first used before 2005 are kept only on evidence of use since then (a
mileage, a postcode area or DVLA activity), while almost all of those first
used since 2005 are in scope through `scope_born`. The newest vehicles are in scope almost
entirely through `scope_born` and DVLA activity, as most have not yet had an
MOT test.
